scope: Complete tools/portable-hosting-kit tree (80 paths), deploy/tor-static, scripts/tor, hosting-kit.yml, tor-static.yml, all deploy/TOR.md variants; recent static-export timestamp change included. findings.title: Failed rollback cleanup can delete the last backup of a previous hosting artifact
findings.condition: Replacing multiple existing output files fails after at least one target has been replaced; restoring that target from its backup also fails, while later removal of the backup succeeds. No attacker prerequisite is needed; a second filesystem error or destination interference suffices.
findings.evidence: rollback() deliberately retains a non-null backup after a failed restore, but commitFilesAtomic() then unconditionally removes every remaining non-null backup in its catch cleanup. packageSite() commits the archive and sidecar through this helper. An error can therefore leave new archive bytes next to an old sidecar while discarding the prior archive recovery copy.
findings.remediation: Track restoration success per target. Preserve any backup whose restore failed, report its exact recovery location together with the original and rollback errors, and remove only temporary files and backups proven redundant after a completed commit or successful restore. Narrow the all-or-nothing/crash-safe documentation to the guarantees actually implemented.
safe_acceptance_criteria: A unit-level fake filesystem can report one commit rename failure and a separate restore rename failure; the original bytes remain available at a reported backup path.
A successful rollback restores old archive and sidecar bytes and removes only redundant temporary paths.
The ordinary success path still publishes matching archive and sidecar bytes.
findings.validation: Source and existing tests were read only. No fault reproduction or test execution performed.

findings.title: Generated operator guide incorrectly groups a subpath with separate browser origins
findings.condition: An operator reads OPERATOR.md packaged by the kit and interprets a subpath mirror as providing independent browser storage or wallet permissions.
findings.evidence: operatorGuide() lists clearnet, onion, I2P, and subpath together as mirror origins with separate storage, sessions, and wallet permissions. The kit README and CLI correctly state that subpaths share an origin and require explicit acknowledgement.
findings.remediation: State that separation is by scheme/host/port. Explicitly say different URL paths on one origin share origin-scoped storage and permissions, preserve the dedicated-origin recommendation, and align generated OPERATOR.md with README and the CLI guard.
safe_acceptance_criteria: Generated operator documentation explicitly states that subpaths on one origin share browser storage and permissions.
Documentation and existing shared-origin refusal/acknowledgement behavior remain consistent.
findings.validation: Documentation and source comparison only. This finding is not a claim of a newly demonstrated browser exploit.

candidates.title: Effective Compose inputs may differ from env-file values checked by selfhost
candidates.evidence: selfhost.envval reads only the selected env file at lines110–118. The helper validates that value for GHOSTPAY_WEB_DIST at146–161 and uses other env-file values for prerequisite checks, but invokes Docker Compose while inheriting ambient environment at280–285 and394–398. Root independently observed Compose variable interpolation for GHOSTPAY_WEB_DIST and image/UID settings.
candidates.condition_to_verify: Determine from official Docker Compose documentation whether an ambient variable can take precedence over the selected env file for these interpolated values. If so, confirm which validated/install destination differs from the effective bind mount or runtime setting.
candidates.owner: Root; official Compose precedence verification pending.
candidates.possible_remediation_if_confirmed: Validate the same resolved Compose configuration that will actually be started, or consistently control environment resolution for prerequisite checks and Compose invocation.
candidates.validation: Static source candidate only; no project execution, runtime verification or vulnerability reproduction performed.
